definition_en: an informal talk between people, or a serious discussion of a subject
core_image: 两人隔桌而坐，话语像球一样来回抛，始终不落地
scene: 咖啡馆里，两个人从天气聊到童年，一小时很快过去。Their conversation lasted until the shop closed.
sceneCN: 这里 conversation 指「交谈」（第 1 个义项：人们之间轻松的谈话）；句意是他们的交谈一直持续到店铺关门。

senses.title: An informal talk
senses.definition: a relaxed talk between two or more people
senses.definitionCN: 两人或多人之间轻松的谈话
senses.example: We had a long conversation about school.
senses.exampleCN: 我们聊了很久学校的事。
senses.why: Two voices taking turns is the oldest way to share a day.
senses.whyCN: 两个声音轮流开口，是分享一天最古老的方式。

senses.title: A serious discussion
senses.definition: a formal discussion of a subject between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体之间就某话题进行的正式讨论
senses.example: The two sides held a conversation on trade.
senses.exampleCN: 双方就贸易问题举行了会谈。
senses.why: When the stakes are high, a talk puts on a formal coat.
senses.whyCN: 事关重大时，谈话就披上了一件正式的外衣。

senses.title: The exchange itself
senses.definition: the act of talking together rather than any single remark
senses.definitionCN: 指一起谈话这一行为，而非某一句单独的话
senses.example: Conversation is how children learn their first words.
senses.exampleCN: 会话是孩子学会最初词汇的方式。
senses.why: A single line is a stone; a conversation is the river.
senses.whyCN: 一句话是一块石头，一次会话是一条河。

intro.en: Conversation comes from Latin conversari, to live or keep company with, built from com-, together, and versare, to turn.
intro.cn: conversation 来自拉丁语 conversari（与人相处、往来），由 com-（一起）与 versare（转动）构成。

items.en: Versare meant to turn something again and again.
items.cn: versare 意为把某物反复转动。

items.en: Conversari meant to live among people and spend time with them.
items.cn: conversari 意为在人群中生活、与人相处。

items.en: Conversatio named a way of life and daily dealings with others.
items.cn: conversatio 指生活方式以及与人的日常往来。

items.en: Old French conversation named a familiar talk between people.
items.cn: 古法语 conversation 指人与人之间的熟络谈话。

items.en: English conversation first meant living or dealing with people.
items.cn: 英语 conversation 最初指与人共同生活或往来。

items.en: Today it means a talk, usually friendly and unhurried.
items.cn: 今天它指一场谈话，通常友好而不慌不忙。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vers-, and the meaning group names other kinds of talk.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vers-，近义组列出其他表示谈话的说法。

connected with talk between people

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two voices taking turns, then move to a formal talk between groups and to conversation as a habit of living.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个声音轮流开口开始，再到团体之间的正式会谈，最后到作为一种生活习性的会话。

normal.en: Con- is together and vers is to turn, so a conversation is words turning between two people.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vers 是转，conversation 就是在两人之间转来转去的话。

normal.en: One mouth alone is a speech; two mouths taking turns make a conversation.
normal.cn: 一张嘴独白是演讲，两张嘴轮流说才是交谈。

normal.en: The word looks like con plus version, as if each answer is a new version of the last.
normal.cn: 这个词看起来像 con 加 version，仿佛每个回答都是对上一句的新版本。

normal.en: A good conversation leaves both people slightly changed.
normal.cn: 一场好的交谈会让两个人都微微改变。

normal.en: No script, no stage: just two chairs turned toward each other.
normal.cn: 没有剧本，没有舞台，只有两把朝向彼此的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a ball of words thrown gently back and forth.
abstract.cn: 想象一团话语被轻轻来回抛接。

abstract.en: Picture two cups on a table and steam rising between them.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两只杯子，热气在两者之间升起。

abstract.en: Picture a river turning at every stone yet never stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河绕过每块石头，却从不停下。

examples.en: They fell into conversation at the bus stop.
examples.cn: 他们在公交站随意聊了起来。

examples.en: I overheard a conversation about the new teacher.
examples.cn: 我无意中听到一段关于新老师的谈话。

examples.en: She keeps a notebook of conversations worth remembering.
examples.cn: 她把值得记住的谈话记在一个本子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conversation 记成 con（一起）加 vers（转）加 ion（名词）：话在两人之间转来转去，就是交谈。

root: 源自拉丁语 conversari（与人相处、往来），由 com-（一起）与 versare（转动）构成，本指共同生活，后专指彼此交谈。

sensesIntro.en: From two voices taking turns, to a formal talk between groups, and at last to the whole habit of talking together.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两个声音轮流开口，到团体之间的正式会谈，最后到一起谈话这一整体习性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball of words thrown gently back and forth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团话语被轻轻来回抛接。

branches.en: A relaxed talk lets two people share an ordinary day.
branches.cn: 轻松的谈话让两个人分享平凡的一天。

branches.en: A formal talk carries weight and often has a purpose.
branches.cn: 正式的会谈有分量，通常带有目的。

branches.en: The habit of talking together is how a language is passed on.
branches.cn: 一起谈话的习性，正是语言得以传递的方式。

branches.en: Both are talk, differing only in tone and setting.
branches.cn: 两者都是谈话，只在语气与场合上不同。

branches.en: A single meeting and a lifelong habit both rest on exchange.
branches.cn: 一次会面与一生的习惯，都建立在交流之上。

intro.en: Conversation is built on Latin com-, together, plus versare, to turn, and the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: conversation 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、versare（转动）与名词词尾 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vers- also runs through convert, reverse and version.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vers- 也贯穿 convert、reverse 与 version。

items.meaning: a talk that turns between people
items.meaningCN: 在人与人之间来回转的谈话

items.example: He wrote in a conversational style.
items.exampleCN: 他用谈话式的风格写作。

items.meaning: to turn something into another form
items.meaningCN: 把某物转成另一种形态
items.example: They convert the barn into a studio.
items.exampleCN: 他们把谷仓改成了工作室。

items.meaning: to turn something the other way
items.exampleCN: 他慢慢地把车倒了回去。

items.meaning: a form turned out from an original
items.meaningCN: 由原作转出的一种形态

definition_en: in a way that reverses what has just been said
core_image: 一枚硬币翻到另一面，图案正好相反
scene: 北边下雪时，南方正晒着太阳，老师让学生把两地说法对调。The north is cold; conversely, the south is warm.
sceneCN: 这里 conversely 指「反过来」（第 1 个义项：引出与上文相反的说法）；句意是北方寒冷，反过来南方温暖。

senses.title: The other way round
senses.definition: used to introduce a statement that reverses the one just made
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出与刚才所说相反的一句话
senses.example: The north is cold; conversely, the south is warm.
senses.exampleCN: 北方寒冷，反过来，南方温暖。
senses.why: A coin has two faces, and naming one calls up the other.
senses.whyCN: 硬币有两面，说出一面就唤起了另一面。

senses.title: In inverse relation
senses.definition: used when two things move in opposite directions
senses.definitionCN: 用于两件事朝相反方向变化的情形
senses.example: Costs fell and, conversely, profits rose.
senses.exampleCN: 成本下降，反之利润上升。
senses.why: A seesaw shows that one end must sink for the other to lift.
senses.whyCN: 跷跷板说明一端必须下沉，另一端才会升起。

intro.en: Conversely is converse plus -ly; converse comes from Latin conversus, turned around, from com-, together, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: conversely 由 converse 加 -ly 构成；converse 来自拉丁语 conversus（转向的），由 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn or change direction.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动或改变方向。

items.en: Conversus described something turned right round.
items.cn: conversus 形容某物被完全转过来。

items.en: English converse meant turned about or opposite.
items.cn: 英语 converse 意为转过来的、相反的。

items.en: The adverb conversely was formed to mark an opposite step in an argument.
items.cn: 副词 conversely 形成，用来在论述中标出一个相反的步骤。

items.en: It now usually opens a sentence that mirrors the one before.
items.cn: 今天它通常引出一个与上一句相对照的句子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vers-, and the meaning group names other ways of stating an opposite.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vers-，近义组列出其他表示相反的说法。

entries.definition: opposite or reversed in order
the act of changing into another form
to turn something the opposite way
in the opposite order or relation
in a contrary manner
in a way that goes against what was said

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a coin turned over, then move to two facts pulling in opposite directions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一枚翻面的硬币开始，再到两件事朝相反方向拉扯。

normal.en: Converse is the opposite side, and -ly makes it an adverb, so conversely means on the opposite side.
normal.cn: converse 是相反的一面，加上 -ly 成为副词，conversely 就是在相反的一面。

normal.en: It always points back at the sentence you just read.
normal.cn: 它总是回头指向你刚读过的那句话。

normal.en: Think of a mirror placed beside a statement.
normal.cn: 想象在一句话旁边立起一面镜子。

normal.en: The signal is simple: the next clause will contradict the last.
normal.cn: 信号很简单：下一个分句会与上一个相反。

normal.en: It is the written cousin of saying on the other hand.
normal.cn: 它是书面语里的另一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a page turned over to show the back.
abstract.cn: 想象把一页纸翻过来露出背面。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows sharing one line and pointing apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两条箭头共用一条线，却指向两边。

abstract.en: Picture a scale tipping the other way.
abstract.cn: 想象天平朝另一边倾斜。

examples.en: The days grew shorter; conversely, the nights grew longer.
examples.cn: 白天变短了，反过来，夜晚变长了。

examples.en: Rich soil holds water well and, conversely, sandy soil drains fast.
examples.cn: 肥沃的土壤保水好，反过来，沙土排水快。

examples.en: Conversely, a quiet room can make a small sound seem loud.
examples.cn: 反过来，安静的房间会让轻微的声音显得很响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conversely 记成 converse（相反的）加 ly：以相反的方式说话，就是反过来。

root: 源自拉丁语 vertere（转）的过去分词 conversus（转过来的），加副词词尾 -ly，表示把话头转到相反的一面。

sensesIntro.en: From a single claim turned over, to two quantities moving in opposite directions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把一句话翻到反面，到两个量朝相反方向变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin flipped to show its other face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币翻过来露出另一面。

branches.en: A statement is reversed and set beside the first.
branches.cn: 一句话被反转，放在第一句旁边。

branches.en: Two quantities move apart, one rising as one falls.
branches.cn: 两个量彼此分开，一个升时一个降。

branches.en: Both uses mark a turn to the opposite side.
branches.cn: 两种用法都标记着转向相反的一面。

branches.en: The adverb keeps the reader from missing the reversal.
branches.cn: 这个副词让读者不会漏掉这次反转。

branches.en: It also signals a fixed inverse link between two facts.
branches.cn: 它也标示两件事之间固定的反向联系。

intro.en: Conversely is converse plus the adverb ending -ly, both resting on Latin vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: conversely 由 converse 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，二者都源于拉丁语 vertere（转）。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vert- also appears in convert, reverse and version.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vert- 也出现在 convert、reverse 与 version 中。

items.exampleCN: 反过来，这条规则可能失效。

items.meaning: able to turn to many uses

items.exampleCN: 版本管理让旧文件保持安全。

definition_zh: 转变；转换；换算；使改变信仰；皈依者
definition_en: to change something into another form or use, or a person who has adopted a new belief
core_image: 一只旧木箱被拆开，重新钉成一张书桌
scene: 老仓库空了许多年，如今门口挂上了书店的牌子。They plan to convert the warehouse into a bookstore.
sceneCN: 这里 convert 指「改造；转变」（第 1 个义项：把某物改成另一种形态或用途）；句意是他们打算把仓库改造成书店。

pos.zh: 转变；转换；换算；使改变信仰

collocations.zh: 把 A 转变成 B

collocations.phrase: a convert to the new method

senses.title: To change form or use
senses.definition: to change something so that it takes a different form or serves a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物，使其呈现另一种形态或有了新用途
senses.example: The barn was converted into a house.
senses.exampleCN: 这座谷仓被改造成了住宅。
senses.why: The same material can serve twice if the shape is changed.
senses.whyCN: 同样的材料，只要改变形状，就能再用一次。

senses.title: To change units or money
senses.definition: to change a value from one system or currency into another
senses.definitionCN: 把数值从一种体系或货币换成另一种
senses.example: You can convert pounds into dollars here.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以在这里把英镑换成美元。
senses.why: Two languages of counting need a bridge, and this verb is that bridge.
senses.whyCN: 两套计数语言之间需要桥，这个动词就是那座桥。

senses.title: A person who has changed belief
senses.definition: someone who has adopted a new religion or set of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 接受了新宗教或新观念的人
senses.example: He became a convert to the new method.
senses.exampleCN: 他转而拥护这种新方法。
senses.why: When a view turns a person around, the person is named after the turn.
senses.whyCN: 当一种看法把一个人转了个方向，人就用这次转向来命名。

intro.en: Convert comes from Latin convertere, to turn about, built from com-, together, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: convert 来自拉丁语 convertere（转过来），由 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, twist or change direction.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动、扭动或改变方向。

items.en: Convertere meant to turn something right round or turn it into another thing.
items.cn: convertere 意为把某物整个转过来，或把它变成另一样东西。

items.en: Conversus, the turned one, described a person or thing changed completely.
items.cn: conversus 指被转过来的人或物，形容彻底改变。

items.en: Old French convertir kept both the physical and the religious senses.
items.cn: 古法语 convertir 同时保留了物理与宗教两种含义。

items.en: English convert first meant to turn from one belief to another.
items.cn: 英语 convert 最初指从一种信仰转向另一种。

items.en: The word now also covers files, fuel and currency.
items.cn: 今天这个词也涵盖文件、燃料与货币的转换。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vert-, and the meaning group names other verbs of change.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vert-，近义组列出其他表示改变的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a box turned into a table, then move to money exchanged and to a person turned toward a new belief.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只箱子变成桌子开始，再到货币兑换，最后到一个人转向新的信仰。

normal.en: Con- is together and vert is to turn, so convert is to turn a thing into a new shape.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vert 是转，convert 就是把东西转成一个新样子。

normal.en: Same wood, new table: nothing is lost, only rearranged.
normal.cn: 同样的木头，新的桌子：什么也没少，只是重新排列。

normal.en: A file becomes a picture, a pound becomes a dollar, a sum becomes a score.
normal.cn: 文件变成图片，英镑变成美元，算式变成得分。

normal.en: The noun convert is a person who has made this turn in belief.
normal.cn: 名词 convert 就是在信仰上完成这次转向的人。

normal.en: Remember the stress moves: con-VERT the verb, CON-vert the person.
normal.cn: 记住重音会移动：动词读 con-VERT，指人时读 CON-vert。

abstract.en: Picture a key melted down and recast as a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被熔化，重新铸成戒指。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows curving into one circle.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头弯成一个圆。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp turned from a dark corner to a bright wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯从暗角转向明亮的墙面。

examples.en: They converted the old factory into flats.
examples.cn: 他们把旧工厂改成了公寓。

examples.en: The app can convert your photos into a short film.
examples.cn: 这个应用能把你的照片转成一段短片。

examples.en: He is a recent convert to cycling.
examples.cn: 他最近成了骑行爱好者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convert 记成 con（一起）加 vert（转）：把原样整个转过去，就是转变与换算。

root: 源自拉丁语 convertere（转过来），由 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成，本指转向，后引申为形态转换与信仰改变。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing turned into a new shape, to values exchanged, and at last to a person turned toward a new belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一件东西被转成新形态，到数值互换，最后到一个人转向新的信仰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old box taken apart and nailed into a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旧箱子被拆开，钉成一张书桌。

branches.en: A building or object is turned to a new purpose.
branches.cn: 一座建筑或一件物品被转向新的用途。

branches.en: A number or a note changes system without losing worth.
branches.cn: 一个数字或一张钞票换了体系，却不失价值。

branches.en: A person turns, and the turn gives the person a new name.
branches.cn: 一个人转了向，这次转向就给了他一个新的称呼。

branches.en: Both are conversions of form, one physical and one abstract.
branches.cn: 两者都是形态转换，一个具体，一个抽象。

branches.en: Money and belief both change hands and change sides.
branches.cn: 金钱与信仰都会换手，也会换边。

intro.en: Convert is built on Latin com-, together, plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: convert 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vert- also runs through reverse, version and versatile.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vert- 也贯穿 reverse、version 与 versatile。

items.meaningCN: 把一种形态变成另一种的装置
items.exampleCN: 转换器发出轻微的嗡声。

definition_en: to make an idea or feeling understood, or to carry something to a place
core_image: 一辆小车沿着窄路，把箱子从这头稳稳送到那头
scene: 她没说一句重话，只用一个眼神就让满屋的人明白了意思。Her silence conveyed more than any speech.
sceneCN: 这里 convey 指「传达」（第 1 个义项：把想法或信息传递给别人）；句意是她的沉默传达的意思胜过任何言语。

senses.title: To make understood
senses.definition: to make an idea or piece of information clear to other people
senses.definitionCN: 使想法或信息被别人清楚地理解
senses.example: Words cannot convey how grateful I am.
senses.exampleCN: 言语无法传达我有多么感激。
senses.why: A thought locked in one head is silent until something carries it out.
senses.whyCN: 锁在一个脑子里的想法是无声的，直到有东西把它运出去。

senses.title: To carry to a place
senses.definition: to take people or goods from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把人或货物从一处送到另一处
senses.example: The pipes convey water to the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这些管道把水送到村里。
senses.why: Before a word could mean to tell, it meant to carry.
senses.whyCN: 在表示告诉之前，这个词先表示搬运。

senses.title: To show a feeling
senses.definition: to let a feeling be seen or felt without stating it plainly
senses.definitionCN: 不必明说，就让某种情感被看见或被感到
senses.example: Her smile conveyed quiet confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的微笑传达出安静的自信。
senses.why: A face can carry a message further than a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 一张脸能把消息送得比一句话更远。

intro.en: Convey comes from Old French conveier, to escort, from Latin conviare, built from com-, together, and via, a way.
intro.cn: convey 来自古法语 conveier（护送），源于拉丁语 conviare，由 com-（一起）与 via（道路）构成。

items.en: Via meant a road or a way through.
items.cn: via 意为道路或通行的路线。

items.en: Conviare meant to travel together along a road.
items.cn: conviare 意为沿路一同行走。

items.en: Old French conveier meant to escort a person on the way.
items.cn: 古法语 conveier 意为在路上护送某人。

items.en: English convey first meant to carry or transport goods.
items.cn: 英语 convey 最初指搬运或运输货物。

items.en: The sense widened to carrying ideas and feelings.
items.cn: 词义扩大，开始指传递想法与情感。

items.en: Today it is used as often for meaning as for goods.
items.cn: 今天它用于含义的频率不亚于用于货物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin way base via-, and the meaning group names other verbs of carrying or telling.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的道路词基 via-，近义组列出其他表示运送或表达的说法。

entries.definition: a group of vehicles travelling together
a machine that carries things along
entries.definitionCN: 沿线路运送东西的机器

entries.definition: a person sent to speak for a country
to make information known to others
to carry goods from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 把货物从一处运到另一处

entries.definition: to show a thought or feeling in words
entries.definitionCN: 用言语表达想法或感情

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a cart on a road, then move to a message crossing a room and to a feeling shown on a face.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从路上的一辆车开始，再到一条消息穿过房间，最后到脸上的表情。

normal.en: Con- is together and vey is a way, so convey is to travel a road with something and hand it over.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vey 是路，convey 就是带着东西走一段路，再交到别人手里。

normal.en: A truck conveys boxes; a sentence conveys a thought.
normal.cn: 卡车运送箱子，句子运送想法。

normal.en: The word hides via, the Latin road, in its last three letters.
normal.cn: 这个词最后三个字母里藏着拉丁语的道路 via。

normal.en: If the listener understands, the delivery has arrived.
normal.cn: 只要听的人懂了，这趟运送就算送到了。

normal.en: A quiet look can convey what shouting cannot.
normal.cn: 一个安静的眼神，能传达喊叫传达不了的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow road with one cart moving steadily.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄路上，一辆小车稳稳前行。

abstract.en: Picture a paper note passed hand to hand across a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条在房间里被一只手传到另一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a warm light carried from one window to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一点暖光从一扇窗被带到下一扇窗。

examples.en: He struggled to convey his excitement in English.
examples.cn: 他努力用英语表达自己的兴奋。

examples.en: The river conveys silt to the plain each spring.
examples.cn: 每年春天，这条河把泥沙运到平原。

examples.en: A short note can convey a great deal of warmth.
examples.cn: 一张短笺能传达许多暖意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convey 记成 con（一起）加 vey（路）：陪着东西走一段路，就是运送，也就是把意思送到别人心里。

root: 源自拉丁语 via（道路），经 conviare（同行）与古法语 conveier（护送）进入英语，本指沿路运送，后引申为传达与表达。

sensesIntro.en: From goods carried along a road, to a thought carried into another mind, and at last to a feeling shown without words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从沿路运送的货物，到送进另一个头脑的想法，最后到不用言语表达的情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cart carrying a box along a narrow road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆小车沿着窄路运送一只箱子。

branches.en: A message crosses the gap between two minds.
branches.cn: 一条消息跨越两个头脑之间的空隙。

branches.en: A pipe or a cart moves real goods to a place.
branches.cn: 管道或车辆把真实货物送到某地。

branches.en: A face or a gesture carries a feeling without words.
branches.cn: 一张脸或一个手势不用言语就带出了情感。

branches.en: Both senses move something inward, one clear and one quiet.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把某种东西送进人心，一个清楚，一个安静。

branches.en: The physical trip came first, and the mental trip borrowed its shape.
branches.cn: 具体的运送先出现，心灵的传递借用了它的形状。

intro.en: Convey is built on Latin com-, together, plus via, a road, through the Old French verb conveier.
intro.cn: convey 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 via（道路）构成，经古法语动词 conveier 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The road base via- also shows in deviate, obvious and envoy.
latinIntro.cn: 道路词基 via- 也出现在 deviate、obvious 与 envoy 中。

items.meaning: the act or means of carrying
items.exampleCN: 公交车是公共交通工具。

items.meaning: a person sent on a way

items.meaning: right in the way, plain to see

definition_en: to decide in a court that someone is guilty, or a person kept in prison for a crime
core_image: 法槌落下，一句判决把被告从席位上推向牢门
scene: 证据摆满桌面，陪审团低声商议后给出了结论。The jury voted to convict him of theft.
sceneCN: 这里 convict 指「判定有罪」（第 1 个义项：法庭认定某人有罪）；句意是陪审团投票认定他犯有盗窃罪。

senses.title: To find guilty
senses.definition: to decide officially in a court that someone has committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 由法庭正式认定某人犯有某项罪行
senses.example: The court convicted him of fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判定他犯有诈骗罪。
senses.why: A court does not say maybe; it says guilty, and the door closes.
senses.whyCN: 法庭不说也许，只说有罪，然后门就关上了。

senses.title: A person in prison
senses.definition: someone who has been found guilty and is serving a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 已被判定有罪并在服刑的人
senses.example: The convict worked in the prison kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 这名囚犯在监狱厨房里干活。
senses.why: A verdict spoken once becomes a name worn for years.
senses.whyCN: 一次宣判说出口，就变成一个要穿很多年的名字。

intro.en: Convict comes from Latin convictus, the past participle of convincere, to prove wrong, built from com-, together, and vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convict 来自拉丁语 convictus，是 convincere（证明有错）的过去分词，由 com-（一起）与 vincere（征服）构成。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer or overcome an opponent.
items.cn: vincere 意为征服或战胜对手。

items.en: Convincere meant to overcome someone with proof.
items.cn: convincere 意为用证据把对方驳倒。

items.en: Convictus described a person overcome by the evidence.
items.cn: convictus 形容被证据压倒的人。

items.en: English convict first meant to prove a person guilty.
items.cn: 英语 convict 最初指证明某人有罪。

items.en: The noun convict named a prisoner sent to a penal colony.
items.cn: 名词 convict 指被送往流放地的囚犯。

items.en: The verb now belongs to courtrooms and the noun to prisons.
items.cn: 今天动词属于法庭，名词属于监狱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin conquering base vict-, and the meaning group names other words for blame and for prisoners.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的征服词基 vict-，近义组列出其他表示判罪与囚犯的词。

entries.definition: a court decision that someone is guilty
to make someone believe something
to force someone out of a place
to say officially that someone is guilty
a person kept in prison
a person who has broken the law

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with proof that beats a denial, then move to the verdict and to the man it names.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从压倒辩解的证据开始，再到那声判决，最后到判决所命名的人。

normal.en: Con- is together and vict is to conquer, so convict is to conquer someone with proof.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vict 是征服，convict 就是用证据把人征服。

normal.en: The same letters name the act and the man: first you convict, then he is a convict.
normal.cn: 同一串字母既指动作也指人：先判定有罪，然后他就成了罪犯。

normal.en: Stress moves like the gavel: con-VICT the act, CON-vict the man.
normal.cn: 重音像法槌一样落下：动作读 con-VICT，指人读 CON-vict。

normal.en: Convict and convince share a base, but proof, not persuasion, puts a person in prison.
normal.cn: convict 与 convince 同根，但把人送进监狱的是证据，不是劝说。

normal.en: A verdict is a sentence that turns a listener into a prisoner.
normal.cn: 一句判决，就是一句把听者变成囚犯的话。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy stamp coming down on a sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚沉重的印章压在一张纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom door closing slowly behind one person.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭的门在一个人身后慢慢关上。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of proof pulling tight around a claim.
abstract.cn: 想象一条证据链在一个说法周围收紧。

examples.en: The jury took three hours to convict her.
examples.cn: 陪审团用了三个小时才判定她有罪。

examples.en: He was convicted of stealing a car.
examples.cn: 他被判犯有偷车罪。

examples.en: The convict had spent ten years inside.
examples.cn: 那名囚犯已经在狱中待了十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convict 记成 con（完全）加 vict（征服）：证据完全把人征服，就是判定有罪。

root: 源自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（一起、完全）与 vincere（征服）构成，本指以证据压倒对方，后指法庭定罪。

sensesIntro.en: From proof that overcomes a denial, to the verdict it produces, and at last to the person that verdict names.
sensesIntro.cn: 从压过辩解的证据，到由此产生的判决，最后到判决所命名的那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gavel falling and a prison door closing.
core.cn: 核心意象：法槌落下，牢门关上。

branches.en: Proof conquers doubt and the court says guilty.
branches.cn: 证据战胜怀疑，法庭宣布有罪。

branches.en: The verdict becomes a label worn by a living person.
branches.cn: 判决变成一个活人身上背着的标签。

branches.en: One word holds both the ruling and the ruled-against.
branches.cn: 一个词同时装着裁决和被裁决的人。

branches.en: The verb needs a court, a charge and a conclusion.
branches.cn: 这个动词需要法庭、指控与结论。

branches.en: The noun needs only a person and a closed door.
branches.cn: 这个名词只需要一个人和一扇关上的门。

intro.en: Convict is built on Latin com-, together or completely, plus vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convict 由拉丁语 com-（一起、完全）与 vincere（征服）构成。

latinIntro.en: The conquering base vict- or vinc- also runs through convince, victory and invincible.
latinIntro.cn: 征服词基 vict- 或 vinc- 也贯穿 convince、victory 与 invincible。

items.meaning: the state of being proven guilty
items.exampleCN: 这项定罪后来被撤销了。

items.meaning: to win someone over by argument
to turn a person out of a place
items.exampleCN: 他们在冬天被赶了出去。

items.example: The victory came at a cost.

items.exampleCN: 没有哪支队伍是不可战胜的。

definition_en: a court decision that someone is guilty, or a strong and steady belief
core_image: 一纸判决放在桌上，胸口另有一只手始终不肯松开
scene: 宣判之后，她仍抬起头，说自己相信这条路是对的。She spoke with the conviction of someone who had waited years.
sceneCN: 这里 conviction 指「坚定信念」（第 2 个义项：深信不疑的看法）；句意是她说话时带着一种等了多年的坚定信念。

senses.title: A court ruling of guilt
senses.definition: an official decision that a person is guilty of a crime
senses.definitionCN: 正式认定某人犯有某项罪行的决定
senses.example: The conviction was overturned on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这项定罪在上诉时被推翻了。
senses.why: A single ruling can follow a person for the rest of a life.
senses.whyCN: 一次裁决可能跟着一个人走过余生。

senses.title: A steady belief
senses.definition: a firm belief that something is true or right
senses.definitionCN: 坚信某事为真或为对的看法
senses.example: She lives by the conviction that work should be fair.
senses.exampleCN: 她秉持工作应当公平的信念生活。
senses.why: A belief that survives argument is held by something stronger than habit.
senses.whyCN: 经得住争辩的信念，靠的比习惯更结实。

intro.en: Conviction comes from Latin convictio, a proving of guilt, from convincere, to overcome with proof, built from com-, together, and vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: conviction 来自拉丁语 convictio（证明有罪），源于 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（一起）与 vincere（征服）构成。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer and to carry the day.
items.cn: vincere 意为征服、占上风。

items.en: Convincere meant to overcome a person by clear proof.
items.cn: convincere 意为用清楚的证据把人驳倒。

items.en: Convictio named both the proof and the state of being proven wrong.
items.cn: convictio 既指证据，也指被证明有错的状态。

items.en: English conviction first meant the proving of guilt.
items.cn: 英语 conviction 最初指对罪行的证明。

items.en: The same word came to mean a belief held beyond doubt.
items.cn: 同一个词开始表示不容怀疑的信念。

items.en: Law keeps the first sense, while daily speech keeps the second.
items.cn: 法律保留了第一个义项，日常口语保留了第二个。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin conquering base vict-, and the meaning group names other words for belief and for legal decisions.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的征服词基 vict-，近义组列出其他表示信念与法律裁决的词。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上判定某人有罪

entries.definition: to make someone feel sure
the act of forcing someone out of a place
a feeling that something is true
a state of being completely sure
the punishment given by a court

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a verdict written down, then move to a belief that cannot be argued away.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一纸写下的判决开始，再到一个争辩不掉的信念。

normal.en: Convict is the act and conviction is the result, so a conviction is what is left after proof has won.
normal.cn: convict 是动作，conviction 是结果：证据赢了之后留下的东西就是定罪。

normal.en: The same word serves the courtroom and the heart.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既服务法庭，也服务人心。

normal.en: Say it with conviction and people lean in; say it without and they look away.
normal.cn: 带着信念说，人会靠近；不带信念说，人会转开目光。

normal.en: -ion turns the verb into a thing you can carry.
normal.cn: -ion 把动词变成一件可以带在身上的东西。

normal.en: A previous conviction is a past that keeps speaking in court.
normal.cn: 前科是一段在法庭上不断开口的过去。

abstract.en: Picture a stamped paper lying beside a closed hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张盖了章的纸，旁边是一只攥紧的手。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that stays lit in a windy room.
abstract.cn: 想象一支在风里也不灭的蜡烛。

abstract.en: Picture a root gripping stone and refusing to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一条根抓住石头，怎么也不松开。

examples.en: He has two previous convictions for theft.
examples.cn: 他有两项盗窃前科。

examples.en: She argued her case with quiet conviction.
examples.cn: 她以平静而坚定的信念为自己的主张辩护。

examples.en: It is my conviction that small steps change a town.
examples.cn: 我深信小小的步伐能改变一座城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conviction 记成 convict（定罪）加 ion：法庭定下的罪，是定罪；心里定下的看法，是信念。

root: 源自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒）的名词 convictio，由 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成，本指证明有罪，后引申为坚定的信念。

sensesIntro.en: From a guilt proven in court, to a belief that proof cannot shake.
sensesIntro.cn: 从法庭上被证明的罪，到证据也摇不动的信念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a verdict sheet beside a tightly closed hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张判决书旁边，是一只攥紧的手。

branches.en: A court writes down what it has proved.
branches.cn: 法庭把已经证明的事写下来。

branches.en: A person holds fast to what argument cannot move.
branches.cn: 一个人紧紧抓住争辩也动不了的东西。

branches.en: Both are things settled beyond easy doubt.
branches.cn: 两者都是不容轻易动摇的定论。

branches.en: The legal sense is public, written and dated.
branches.cn: 法律义项是公开的、书面的、有日期的。

branches.en: The personal sense is quiet, inward and unrecorded.
branches.cn: 个人义项是安静的、向内的、不被记录的。

intro.en: Conviction is convict plus -ion, resting on Latin convincere, to overcome with proof.
intro.cn: conviction 是 convict 加 -ion，根源是拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒）。

latinIntro.en: The conquering base vict- or vinc- also runs through convince, victory and invincible.
latinIntro.cn: 征服词基 vict- 或 vinc- 也贯穿 convince、victory 与 invincible。

items.meaningCN: 已经定下的裁决或信念

items.meaning: to win someone to a belief
items.meaningCN: 把某人争取到某种看法上

items.exampleCN: 那位冠军看起来不可战胜。

definition_en: to make someone believe that something is true, or to persuade someone to act
core_image: 一个人把一条清楚的路指给另一个人看，对方终于点头
scene: 她拿出一张张照片，父亲看完后不再反对。The photos convinced him that the plan was safe.
sceneCN: 这里 convince 指「使确信」（第 1 个义项：让某人相信某事为真）；句意是这些照片使他确信这个计划是安全的。

derivatives.zh: 有说服力的；令人信服的

senses.title: To make someone sure
senses.definition: to cause someone to believe that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 使某人相信某事为真
senses.example: The evidence convinced her that he was honest.
senses.exampleCN: 证据使她确信他是诚实的。
senses.why: Doubt is a door held shut, and proof is the hand that opens it.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑是一扇关着的门，证据就是推开它的那只手。

senses.title: To persuade into action
senses.definition: to talk someone into doing something
senses.definitionCN: 通过劝说使某人去做某事
senses.example: He convinced his parents to let him travel.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服父母让他去旅行。
senses.why: Belief is half the work; the other half is a step taken.
senses.whyCN: 相信只算一半，另一半是迈出那一步。

intro.en: Convince comes from Latin convincere, to overcome with proof, built from com-, together, and vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convince 来自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（一起、完全）与 vincere（征服）构成。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer an opponent in a struggle.
items.cn: vincere 意为在较量中战胜对手。

items.en: Convincere meant to defeat someone with reasons rather than force.
items.cn: convincere 意为用道理而非武力把人驳倒。

items.en: English convince first meant to prove a person wrong.
items.cn: 英语 convince 最初指证明某人有错。

items.en: The meaning softened to making someone feel certain.
items.cn: 词义变柔和，转为使某人感到确定。

items.en: A new pattern, convince someone to do, became common.
items.cn: convince someone to do 这一新搭配变得常见。

items.en: Today it covers both belief and action.
items.cn: 今天它同时涵盖相信与行动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin conquering base vinc-, and the meaning group names other ways of bringing someone to a view.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的征服词基 vinc-，近义组列出其他使人接受看法的说法。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上判定某人有罪

entries.definition: able to make people believe
too strong to be beaten
to make someone agree to do something
to tell someone firmly so doubt goes away
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地告诉某人以消除疑虑

entries.definition: to give someone enough reason to accept
entries.definitionCN: 给某人足够的理由接受

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with proof winning a mind, then move to a person moving from doubt to a decision.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从证据赢下一个头脑开始，再到一个人从怀疑走向决定。

normal.en: Con- is completely and vince is to conquer, so convince is to conquer doubt completely.
normal.cn: con- 是完全，vince 是征服，convince 就是把怀疑彻底征服。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with convict: one changes a mind, the other closes a door.
normal.cn: 别和 convict 搞混：一个改变想法，一个关上牢门。

normal.en: You convince a friend; you convict a defendant.
normal.cn: 你说服朋友；你给被告定罪。

normal.en: The adjective convincing adds -ing, as if the argument is still working on you.
normal.cn: 形容词 convincing 加了 -ing，仿佛那套论证还在你身上起作用。

normal.en: A convinced person walks differently from a merely informed one.
normal.cn: 确信的人走路的姿态，和仅仅被告知的人不一样。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate opening after a key turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙转动后，锁着的门开了。

abstract.en: Picture a scale slowly settling on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象天平慢慢落向一边。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing down a clear road at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏里一只手指出一条清楚的路。

examples.en: Nothing you say will convince me otherwise.
examples.cn: 你说什么也无法使我相信别的。

examples.en: She convinced the class to join the clean-up.
examples.cn: 她说服全班参加清洁活动。

examples.en: His explanation was simple and convincing.
examples.cn: 他的解释简单而有说服力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convince 记成 con（完全）加 vince（征服）：把对方的怀疑完全征服，就是使确信、说服。

root: 源自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成，本指以理服人，后指使确信与说服。

sensesIntro.en: From proof winning a mind, to a mind deciding to move.
sensesIntro.cn: 从证据赢下一个头脑，到这个头脑决定行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pointing down a clear road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一条清楚的路。

branches.en: Evidence settles the question of what is true.
branches.cn: 证据解决了什么为真这个问题。

branches.en: A settled mind then agrees to act.
branches.cn: 安定的心随后同意行动。

branches.en: Belief and action are two halves of one movement.
branches.cn: 相信与行动是同一个动作的两半。

branches.en: The first sense is about truth and evidence.
branches.cn: 第一个义项关乎真相与证据。

branches.en: The second is about will and permission.
branches.cn: 第二个义项关乎意愿与许可。

intro.en: Convince is built on Latin com-, completely, plus vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convince 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成。

latinIntro.en: The conquering base vinc- also runs through convict, victory and invincible.
latinIntro.cn: 征服词基 vinc- 也贯穿 convict、victory 与 invincible。

items.exampleCN: 随后是一场令人信服的胜利。

items.meaning: the gaining of the upper hand

items.exampleCN: 他们觉得自己不可战胜。

items.meaning: to put a person out by force

definition_en: to prepare food with heat, a person who prepares food, or to change records dishonestly
core_image: 灶上锅盖掀起，白汽带着香味散满整个厨房
scene: 放学回家，锅里的汤正咕嘟作响。My father is cooking dinner in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 cook 指「烹饪」（第 1 个义项：用加热的方式做食物）；句意是我父亲正在厨房做晚饭。

senses.title: To prepare food with heat
senses.definition: to make food ready to eat by heating it
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热使食物可以食用
senses.example: She cooked rice for thirty people.
senses.exampleCN: 她为三十个人煮了米饭。
senses.why: Fire turns raw things into a meal and a house into a home.
senses.whyCN: 火把生的东西变成一餐饭，也把房子变成家。

senses.title: A person who prepares food
senses.definition: someone whose job is preparing meals
senses.definitionCN: 以做饭为职业的人
senses.example: The cook came out to greet us.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师走出来迎接我们。
senses.why: The act and the person share one short word in English.
senses.whyCN: 在英语里，这个动作和这个人共用一个短短的单词。

senses.title: To falsify records
senses.definition: to change numbers or accounts in order to cheat
senses.definitionCN: 为了作弊而改动数字或账目
senses.example: They were caught cooking the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 他们篡改账目被抓住了。
senses.why: Bad numbers are like raw food: someone cooks them to make them look finished.
senses.whyCN: 假数字像生食材：有人把它煮过，好让它看起来已经做好。

intro.en: Cook comes from Old English coc, a cook, borrowed from Latin coquus, from coquere, to cook or ripen.
intro.cn: cook 来自古英语 coc（厨师），借自拉丁语 coquus，源于 coquere（煮、使成熟）。

items.en: Coquere meant to cook, boil or ripen food.
items.cn: coquere 意为煮、煮开或使食物成熟。

items.en: Coquus named the person who did this work.
items.cn: coquus 指做这项工作的人。

items.en: Old English coc meant a cook in a household.
items.cn: 古英语 coc 指家中的厨师。

items.en: The same word began to serve as a verb as well.
items.cn: 同一个词也开始当动词用。

items.en: Cooking became a common topic in printed household books.
items.cn: 烹饪成为印行家政书中的常见话题。

items.en: The slang sense of falsifying accounts appeared much later.
items.cn: 篡改账目的俚语义项出现得晚得多。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cook- base, and the meaning group names other words for preparing food.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 cook- 词基，近义组列出其他表示做饭的词。

entries.definition: a machine or pot for cooking food
the skill of preparing food
a small sweet biscuit
a trained cook in a restaurant

entries.definition: to get food ready to be eaten
entries.definitionCN: 把食物准备好以供食用

entries.definition: to cook food in an oven

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a pot steaming on a stove, then move to the person at the stove and to numbers quietly altered.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从灶上冒汽的锅开始，再到灶边的人，最后到被悄悄改动的数字。

normal.en: Cook is a verb and a noun at once: the cook cooks.
normal.cn: cook 既是动词又是名词：厨师做饭。

normal.en: The word is as short as a quick stir of the spoon.
normal.cn: 这个词和快搅一下勺子一样短。

normal.en: Cook a meal for guests, and the house smells warm.
normal.cn: 给客人做一顿饭，屋里就有了暖味。

normal.en: Cook the books and the warmth turns to smoke.
normal.cn: 篡改账目，这股暖意就变成了烟。

normal.en: Remember the -er words: cooker is the stove, cookery is the skill.
normal.cn: 记住带 -er 的词：cooker 是炉灶，cookery 是技艺。

abstract.en: Picture steam lifting a lid and curling toward a window.
abstract.cn: 想象蒸汽顶起锅盖，卷向窗户。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon tasting soup in a bright kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象明亮的厨房里，一把勺子尝着汤。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with one figure written over another.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿上，一个数字盖住了另一个。

examples.en: He cooked noodles for the whole team.
examples.cn: 他给全队煮了面条。

examples.en: My grandmother is the best cook I know.
examples.cn: 我奶奶是我认识的最好的厨师。

examples.en: The manager was accused of cooking the figures.
examples.cn: 经理被指控篡改数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cook 记成一口锅的咕嘟声：锅一响，饭就熟了，做这件事的人也叫 cook。

root: 源自拉丁语 coquere（煮、使成熟），经 coquus（厨师）借入古英语作 coc，动词与名词同形，后引申出篡改账目的俚语义。

sensesIntro.en: From a pot of food over fire, to the person beside it, and at last to numbers cooked to hide the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 从火上的一锅食物，到锅边的人，最后到被烹煮以掩盖真相的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pot lid lifting with a cloud of steam.
core.cn: 核心意象：锅盖被一团蒸汽顶起。

branches.en: Heat changes raw food into a meal.
branches.cn: 加热把生食变成一餐饭。

branches.en: A person can be named by the work of the hands.
branches.cn: 一个人可以用双手的活计来称呼。

branches.en: False figures are prepared like food, to look ready.
branches.cn: 假数字像食物一样被加工，好显得已经做好。

branches.en: The act and its doer share one plain word.
branches.cn: 动作与做动作的人共用一个朴素的词。

branches.en: Both senses are about making something presentable.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎把东西弄得像样。

intro.en: Cook rests on Latin coquere, to cook or ripen, which reached English through Old English coc.
intro.cn: cook 源于拉丁语 coquere（煮、使成熟），经古英语 coc 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The cooking base coqu- also shows in cuisine, concoct and biscuit.
latinIntro.cn: 烹饪词基 coqu- 也出现在 cuisine、concoct 与 biscuit 中。

items.meaning: to cook up a mixture or a story
items.meaningCN: 把材料煮成一体，也指编造

definition_en: a device or pot used for cooking, or a fruit that is good for cooking
core_image: 厨房角落一台白色炉灶，四个灶眼像四只安静的圆眼
scene: 搬进新家那天，母亲第一件事是擦净厨房里的炉灶。She cleaned the cooker before unpacking the plates.
sceneCN: 这里 cooker 指「炉灶；炊具」（第 1 个义项：用来烹煮食物的器具）；句意是她先擦净炉灶，再拆开盘子。

collocations.phrase: put the pot on the cooker

senses.title: A device for cooking
senses.definition: a machine or large pot that is used to cook food
senses.definitionCN: 用来烹煮食物的机器或大锅
senses.example: The cooker has four rings and a small oven.
senses.exampleCN: 这台炉灶有四个灶眼和一个小烤箱。
senses.why: The tool takes the name of the act it exists to serve.
senses.whyCN: 工具借用了它生来要服务的那个动作的名字。

senses.title: A fruit for cooking
senses.definition: a fruit, especially an apple, grown to be cooked rather than eaten raw
senses.definitionCN: 专门用于烹煮而非生吃的水果，尤指苹果
senses.example: These cookers are too sour to eat raw.
senses.exampleCN: 这些煮食苹果太酸，不能生吃。
senses.why: Some fruit is grown for the pot, not for the hand.
senses.whyCN: 有些水果是为锅种的，不是为手种的。

intro.en: Cooker is cook plus the agent ending -er, which first named a person and later the machine.
intro.cn: cooker 是 cook 加施事词尾 -er，最初指人，后来指机器。

items.en: Coc named the person who prepared food.
items.cn: coc 指准备食物的人。

items.en: The verb coken described the work done at the fire.
items.cn: 动词 coken 描述在火边干的活。

items.en: Cooker first meant a person employed to cook.
items.cn: cooker 最初指受雇做饭的人。

items.en: With new kitchen machines, cooker shifted to the device itself.
items.cn: 随着厨房机器出现，cooker 转指器具本身。

items.en: Compounds like rice cooker and slow cooker are now common.
items.cn: rice cooker 与 slow cooker 之类的复合词如今很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cook- base, and the meaning group names other kitchen words for heat and cooking.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 cook- 词基，近义组列出其他与加热和烹煮有关的厨房词。

entries.definition: to prepare food with heat
the skill of preparing food
a small sweet biscuit
a device with burners for cooking
a closed box for baking food
entries.definitionCN: 用来烘烤食物的封闭箱体

entries.definition: a large cooker with an oven

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stove in a new kitchen, then move to fruit grown for the pot.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从新厨房里的一台炉灶开始，再到为锅而种的水果。

normal.en: Cook plus -er makes the thing that cooks, just as print plus -er makes the printer.
normal.cn: cook 加 -er 就是会煮东西的物件，正如 print 加 -er 是打印机。

normal.en: A cook is a person; a cooker is a machine.
normal.cn: cook 是人，cooker 是机器。

normal.en: In British homes the cooker is the whole stove, not just one pot.
normal.cn: 在英国家里，cooker 指整台炉灶，而不只是一口锅。

normal.en: Rice cooker and slow cooker show the word at work in compounds.
normal.cn: rice cooker 与 slow cooker 展示了这个词在复合词中的用法。

normal.en: A cooker apple is named for what will happen to it, not for how it tastes raw.
normal.cn: 煮食苹果是按它将要经历的事命名的，不是按生吃的味道。

abstract.en: Picture four round burners glowing in a dark kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象暗厨房里四个圆形灶眼发着光。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy lid rattling on a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的锅盖在锅上轻轻震动。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of sour apples beside a saucepan.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮酸苹果放在深锅旁边。

examples.en: She wiped the cooker after every meal.
examples.cn: 她每顿饭后都擦一遍炉灶。

examples.en: A rice cooker saves time on busy evenings.
examples.cn: 忙碌的晚上，电饭锅能省下时间。

examples.en: The old cooker gave off a smell of gas.
examples.cn: 那台旧炉灶散发出煤气味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cooker 记成 cook（煮）加 er（东西）：用来煮东西的物件，就是炉灶与炊具。

root: 由 cook（烹饪）加施事词尾 -er 构成，本指做饭的人，十九世纪起转指炉灶等炊事器具。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who cooks, to the machine that does the work, and to fruit meant for the pot.
sensesIntro.cn: 从做饭的人，到承担这项工作的机器，再到为锅而种的水果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white stove with four quiet burners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台有四个安静灶眼的白色炉灶。

branches.en: A machine holds the heat that cooks the meal.
branches.cn: 机器承住热量，把饭煮熟。

branches.en: A fruit is chosen for the pot rather than the plate.
branches.cn: 一种水果被选中进锅，而不是上盘生吃。

branches.en: Both senses tie an object to the act of cooking.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把某样东西系在烹煮这个动作上。

branches.en: The device sense grew from the older word for a person.
branches.cn: 器具义项是从更早指人的词义长出来的。

branches.en: The fruit sense is local and survives mainly in British speech.
branches.cn: 水果义项较地方化，主要保留在英式说法里。

intro.en: Cooker is cook plus -er, the old ending for a person or thing that does an action.
intro.cn: cooker 是 cook 加 -er，这个古老词尾表示做某动作的人或物。

latinIntro.en: The cooking base coqu- also shows in cuisine, concoct and biscuit.

pos.zh: 网络小甜饼；网站存下的数据文件

derivatives.zh: 千篇一律的；按模子做的

senses.title: A small sweet biscuit
senses.definition: a small flat cake baked until crisp and sweet
senses.definitionCN: 烤得酥脆香甜的小块扁饼
senses.example: She left a plate of cookies on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她在桌上留了一盘饼干。
senses.why: A small round thing can carry more warmth than a whole meal.
senses.whyCN: 一块圆圆的小东西，能比一整餐饭更暖人心。

senses.title: A file stored by a website
senses.definition: a small piece of data a website keeps on a visitor's computer

senses.exampleCN: 这个网站用一段小数据记住你的名字。
senses.why: The sweet name hides a small memory kept for the next visit.
senses.whyCN: 这个甜甜的名字背后，是一份留给下次来访的小记忆。

senses.title: A tough person

intro.en: Cookie comes from Dutch koekje, a little cake, the diminutive of koek, cake.
intro.cn: cookie 来自荷兰语 koekje（小饼），是 koek（饼）的指小形式。

items.en: Koek meant a flat baked cake.
items.cn: koek 意为烤成的扁饼。

items.en: Koekje was the small, affectionate form of koek.
items.cn: koekje 是 koek 的指小形式，带有亲切意味。

items.en: Dutch settlers brought the word into American English.
items.cn: 荷兰移民把这个词带进了美国英语。

items.en: Cookie settled as the everyday word, beside British biscuit.
items.cn: cookie 成为美式日常用词，与英式 biscuit 并存。

items.en: The computing sense appeared in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 计算机领域的义项在二十世纪后期出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cook- base, and the meaning group names other baked sweet foods.

definition_en: slightly cold, calm and controlled, fashionable, or to make something less warm
core_image: 夏夜的风穿过窗纱，桌上水杯的外壁凝出细水珠
scene: 争执到最响的时候，他只是把声音放低。Try to stay cool when everyone else is shouting.
sceneCN: 这里 cool 指「冷静的」（第 2 个义项：镇静而不被情绪带走）；句意是当别人都在大喊时，尽量保持冷静。

senses.title: Slightly cold
senses.definition: pleasantly low in temperature, not cold enough to hurt
senses.definitionCN: 温度宜人偏低，尚未冷到难受
senses.example: A cool wind came off the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面上吹来一阵凉风。
senses.why: The body sighs with relief when heat steps back a little.
senses.whyCN: 热气稍稍退开，身体就松了一口气。

senses.title: Calm under pressure
senses.definition: not excited, angry or frightened in a difficult moment
senses.definitionCN: 在困难时刻不激动、不发怒、不惊慌
senses.example: She stayed cool while the others argued.
senses.exampleCN: 别人争吵时她保持冷静。
senses.why: A cool head is a warm heart kept under control.
senses.whyCN: 冷静的头脑，是被管住的热心肠。

senses.title: Fashionable and admired
senses.definition: very fashionable, impressive or approved of by others
senses.definitionCN: 非常时髦、令人印象深刻或被人认可的
senses.example: That old bike is still cool.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧自行车还是很酷。
senses.why: What is admired keeps a distance, and distance feels cool.
senses.whyCN: 被欣赏的东西总保持一点距离，而距离感就是凉意。

intro.en: Cool comes from Old English col, cold, from a Germanic root shared with cold itself.
intro.cn: cool 来自古英语 col（冷的），词根与 cold 同属日耳曼语族。

items.en: A root meaning cold lay behind words in several northern languages.
items.cn: 一个意为冷的词根藏在几种北方语言里。

items.en: Col meant moderately cold, milder than cold.
items.cn: col 意为适度地冷，比 cold 温和。

items.en: The word extended from air to drink and to temper.
items.cn: 这个词从空气扩展到饮料，再扩展到脾气。

items.en: Cool gained the sense of calm and self-controlled.
items.cn: cool 获得了冷静、自制的含义。

items.en: Jazz and youth culture gave it the sense of stylish.
items.cn: 爵士乐与青年文化赋予它时髦的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same cool base, and the meaning group names nearby ideas of cold and calm.
note.cn: 形近组由同一个 cool 词基构成，近义组列出与冷和冷静相近的说法。

entries.definition: a box or device that keeps things cold
entries.definitionCN: 让东西保持低温的箱子或装置

entries.definition: in a calm or unfriendly way
the state of being cool
uncomfortably cold
peaceful and not excited
following the style of the moment

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a breeze on a warm evening, then move to a head that keeps its balance and to a style others copy.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从暖夜里的微风开始，再到一颗保持平衡的脑袋，最后到别人模仿的风格。

normal.en: One short word covers temperature, temper and taste.
normal.cn: 一个短短的单词，同时管温度、脾气和品味。

normal.en: Cool weather cools a drink, and a cool head cools a quarrel.
normal.cn: 凉爽的天气让饮料变凉，冷静的头脑让争吵降温。

normal.en: Compare cool with cold: cool is the pleasant side of cold.
normal.cn: 把 cool 和 cold 比一比：cool 是冷里让人舒服的那一面。

normal.en: To play it cool is to keep the face calm while the heart races.
normal.cn: play it cool 就是心里乱跳，脸上却平静。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb share one shape, so the wind cools the room.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词同形，于是风把房间吹凉。

abstract.en: Picture a glass sweating on a table in July.
abstract.cn: 想象七月里桌上一只冒水珠的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a lake surface with no ripple at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时没有一丝波纹的湖面。

abstract.en: Picture someone leaning back while others lean in.
abstract.cn: 想象别人都向前倾时，有个人向后靠着。

examples.en: The evening air turned cool after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后傍晚的空气变凉了。

examples.en: He kept cool and answered every question slowly.
examples.cn: 他保持冷静，慢慢回答了每个问题。

examples.en: Let the soup cool before you taste it.
examples.cn: 让汤凉一点再尝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cool 记成一口凉气：温度退一步是凉爽，情绪退一步是冷静，风格退一步就成了酷。

root: 源自日耳曼语中意为冷的词根，古英语作 col，本指适度寒冷，后引申为冷静自制，二十世纪又引申为时髦。

sensesIntro.en: From air that is pleasantly cold, to a temper held steady, and at last to a style others admire.
sensesIntro.cn: 从宜人微凉的空气，到稳稳管住的脾气，最后到别人欣赏的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cool breeze moving through a warm room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一阵凉风穿过温热的房间。

branches.en: A lower temperature brings comfort.
branches.cn: 更低的温度带来舒适。

branches.en: A steady mind keeps its balance in noise.
branches.cn: 沉稳的心在喧闹里保持平衡。

branches.en: Admired style borrows the word for pleasant distance.
branches.cn: 被人欣赏的风格，借用了这种舒服的距离感。

branches.en: Both rest on a step back from heat.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在从热里退后一步。

branches.en: Calm and cool style both look unbothered.
branches.cn: 冷静与酷的风格，看起来都不慌不忙。

intro.en: Cool is a native Germanic word, and its family grows with -er, -ly, -ness and -ing.
intro.cn: cool 是本族日耳曼词，它的家族由 -er、-ly、-ness 与 -ing 扩展而来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base for cold, frig-, appears in fridge, frigid and refrigerant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示冷的词基 frig- 出现在 fridge、frigid 与 refrigerant 中。

items.meaning: a container that keeps things cold
items.meaningCN: 让东西保持低温的容器
items.example: Put the milk in the cooler.

items.meaning: the act of making less warm
a fluid that carries heat away

items.exampleCN: 这首歌如今听起来不酷了。

items.example: A cool-headed driver avoided the crash.
items.exampleCN: 一位冷静的司机避免了一场撞车。

definition_en: to work together with others for a shared aim, or to do what is asked of you
core_image: 两双手同时抬起同一只箱子，脚步踩在一个节拍上
scene: 谁也不肯先动，老师只好请两个小组一起想办法。The two teams agreed to cooperate on the project.
sceneCN: 这里 cooperate 指「合作」（第 1 个义项：为共同目标一起做事）；句意是两个小组同意在这个项目上合作。

senses.title: To work together
senses.definition: to join with others in doing something for a shared aim
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起为共同目标做某事
senses.example: The two schools cooperate on a summer camp.
senses.exampleCN: 两所学校在夏令营上合作。
senses.why: One pair of hands can lift only so much; four hands lift the rest.
senses.whyCN: 一双手能抬起的有限，另外两双手抬起剩下的。

senses.title: To go along with a request
senses.definition: to do what someone in authority asks, without resisting
senses.definitionCN: 按当权者的要求去做，不加抗拒
senses.example: Please cooperate with the officer at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 请配合门口的工作人员。
senses.why: Sometimes working together means simply not pushing back.
senses.whyCN: 有时合作就是干脆不往回推。

intro.en: Cooperate comes from Late Latin cooperari, built from co-, together, and operari, to work, from opus, work.
intro.cn: cooperate 来自晚期拉丁语 cooperari，由 co-（一起）与 operari（工作）构成，词根 opus 意为工作。

items.en: Opus meant work, a task or a piece of labour.
items.cn: opus 意为工作、任务或一份劳动。

items.en: Operari meant to work or to be busy with a task.
items.cn: operari 意为工作或忙于某项任务。

items.en: Cooperari meant to work along with another person.
items.cn: cooperari 意为与另一个人一起工作。

items.en: English cooperate first described working jointly on a task.
items.cn: 英语 cooperate 最初指共同做一项工作。

items.en: The word gained the milder sense of agreeing to help.
items.cn: 这个词又获得了同意协助这一较温和的含义。

items.en: Today it covers teams, machines and even countries.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖团队、机器，甚至国家。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin working base oper-, and the meaning group names other ways of acting with others.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的工作词基 oper-，近义组列出其他与他人共同行动的说法。

entries.definition: to work or to make a machine work
the act of working together
willing to work with others
to work closely with someone on a project
entries.definitionCN: 与某人在项目上紧密合作

entries.definition: to help someone with a task
entries.definitionCN: 在某项任务上帮助某人

entries.definition: to join together for a common end

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two pairs of hands on one box, then move to a person agreeing to help.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两双手抬起同一只箱子开始，再到一个人同意协助。

normal.en: Co- means together and operate means to work, so cooperate is to work together.
normal.cn: co- 是一起，operate 是工作，cooperate 就是一起工作。

normal.en: Two people carry a table more easily than one, and the word is built for that picture.
normal.cn: 两个人抬桌子比一个人轻松，这个词就是为这幅画面造的。

normal.en: Say it as co-operate and the meaning appears by itself.
normal.cn: 把它读作 co-operate，意思自己就出来了。

normal.en: A cooperative person makes the room lighter.
normal.cn: 一个愿意配合的人，会让整个房间轻松起来。

normal.en: Even machines cooperate: two gears turn each other.
normal.cn: 连机器也会合作：两个齿轮彼此带动。

abstract.en: Picture two hands lifting the same heavy box.
abstract.cn: 想象两双手抬起同一只重箱子。

abstract.en: Picture two rivers meeting and sharing one bed.
abstract.cn: 想象两条河汇合，共用一条河床。

abstract.en: Picture a door opened from both sides at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门同时从两边被推开。

examples.en: We must cooperate if the plan is to work.
examples.cn: 若要让计划奏效，我们必须合作。

examples.en: She cooperated with the police without hesitation.
examples.cn: 她毫不犹豫地配合了警方。

examples.en: The two labs cooperate closely on this research.
examples.cn: 这两个实验室在这项研究上密切合作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cooperate 记成 co（一起）加 operate（工作）：一起干活，就是合作。

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 cooperari（一同工作），由 co-（一起）与 operari（工作）构成，词根 opus 意为工作。

sensesIntro.en: From hands lifting one load together, to a person choosing not to resist.
sensesIntro.cn: 从几双手一同抬起一份重物，到一个人选择不加抗拒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pairs of hands raising one box.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双手抬起同一只箱子。

branches.en: People pool effort toward one shared aim.
branches.cn: 人们把力气汇向同一个目标。

branches.en: A person simply lets the request be carried out.
branches.cn: 一个人干脆让那个要求被顺利执行。

branches.en: Both senses lower the friction between people.
branches.cn: 两个义项都减少了人与人之间的摩擦。

branches.en: The first sense needs a common purpose.
branches.cn: 第一个义项需要一个共同的目的。

branches.en: The second needs only a willing response.
branches.cn: 第二个义项只需要一个愿意的回应。

intro.en: Cooperate is built on Latin co-, together, plus operari, to work.
intro.cn: cooperate 由拉丁语 co-（一起）与 operari（工作）构成。

latinIntro.en: The working base oper- also appears in operate, operation and opus.
latinIntro.cn: 工作词基 oper- 也出现在 operate、operation 与 opus 中。

items.meaning: to work or run a machine
the act of working or running
a person who runs a machine
items.exampleCN: 操作员挥手让我们过去。
那部大提琴作品很有名。

definition_zh: 协调；使配合；坐标；同等的
definition_en: to make different parts work well together, a position on a map, or equal in rank
core_image: 几路人马在同一张时间表上对齐，指针同时指向一处
scene: 几支队伍先后赶来，负责人先把时间和路线排好。She coordinated the rescue from a small tent.
sceneCN: 这里 coordinate 指「协调」（第 1 个义项：让不同部分配合起来）；句意是她在一个小帐篷里协调这次救援。

senses.title: To bring parts into step
senses.definition: to arrange different people or parts so that they work well together
senses.definitionCN: 安排不同的人或部分，使其配合良好
senses.example: She coordinated the work of four teams.
senses.exampleCN: 她协调了四个团队的工作。
senses.why: Separate clocks tell separate times until one hand sets them all.
senses.whyCN: 各自走时的钟各说各话，直到有一只手把它们调齐。

senses.title: A position on a grid
senses.definition: one of the numbers that fix a point on a map or graph
senses.definitionCN: 在地图或图表上确定一个点的数值之一
senses.example: The ship sent its coordinates by radio.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船用无线电发出了坐标。
senses.why: Two numbers can pin down one exact spot in a wide world.
senses.whyCN: 两个数字就能在广阔世界里钉住一个确切的点。

senses.title: Equal in rank
senses.definition: having the same level or importance as another thing
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物处于相同层级或同等重要
senses.example: The two clauses are coordinate in grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个分句在语法上是并列的。
senses.why: Things set side by side stand on one level.
senses.whyCN: 并排放置的东西，站在同一个高度上。

intro.en: Coordinate comes from Latin co-, together, and ordinare, to arrange, from ordo, order or row.
intro.cn: coordinate 来自拉丁语 co-（一起）与 ordinare（排列），词根 ordo 意为次序、行列。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, a rank or a settled order.
items.cn: ordo 意为行列、等级或既定次序。

items.en: Ordinare meant to set things in rows and put them in order.
items.cn: ordinare 意为把事物排成行、理出次序。

items.en: Coordinare meant to arrange several things together.
items.cn: coordinare 意为把几样事物一同排列。

items.en: English coordinate first described things of equal rank.
items.cn: 英语 coordinate 最初形容等级相同的事物。

items.en: Mathematics gave the noun the sense of a fixed position.
items.cn: 数学赋予这个名词固定位置的含义。

items.en: The verb now mostly means to bring work into step.
items.cn: 今天动词主要表示把工作安排得彼此合拍。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ordering base ordin-, and the meaning group names other verbs of making things fit.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的排列词基 ordin-，近义组列出其他使事物相合的说法。

entries.definition: the act of making parts work together
entries.definitionCN: 让各部分配合起来的做法

entries.definition: a person who brings work together
lower in rank than another
to arrange things into a working whole

entries.definition: to make things happen at the same time
to bring things into a straight line or agreement

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with several clocks set to one time, then move to numbers fixing a spot and to things standing level.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从几只被调成同一时间的钟开始，再到确定位置的数字，最后到站在同一高度的事物。

normal.en: Co- is together and ordinate is arranged in order, so coordinate is to put things in one order.
normal.cn: co- 是一起，ordinate 是排成次序，coordinate 就是把事物排进同一个次序。

normal.en: Think of a conductor who never plays a note but keeps everyone together.
normal.cn: 想象一位指挥家，自己不奏一个音，却让所有人合在一起。

normal.en: Two numbers on a map are also a kind of order.
normal.cn: 地图上的两个数字，也是一种次序。

normal.en: The same word means to arrange and to stand at the same level.
normal.cn: 同一个词既表示安排，也表示处在同一层级。

normal.en: Remember co- means together in all three senses.
normal.cn: 记住三个义项里都藏着 co- 的一起。

abstract.en: Picture four clocks hung in a row, all showing one time.
abstract.cn: 想象四只钟挂成一排，都指向同一个时间。

abstract.en: Picture a cross on a map with two numbers beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一个十字，旁边写着两个数字。

abstract.en: Picture two blocks placed side by side at one height.
abstract.cn: 想象两块积木并排放在同一高度。

examples.en: She coordinated the whole event by phone.
examples.cn: 她通过电话协调了整个活动。

examples.en: Write down the coordinates before you move.
examples.cn: 行动之前先把坐标记下来。

examples.en: The two departments work as coordinate units.
examples.cn: 这两个部门作为同级单位合作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coordinate 记成 co（一起）加 ordin（次序）加 ate：把事情排进同一个次序，就是协调。

root: 源自拉丁语 coordinare（一同排列），由 co-（一起）与 ordinare（排列）构成，词根 ordo 意为次序，后兼指坐标与同级。

sensesIntro.en: From clocks set to one time, to numbers fixing a spot, and at last to things standing on one level.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被调成同一时间的钟，到确定一个点的数字，最后到站在同一层级的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several hands setting clocks to one time.
core.cn: 核心意象：几只手把钟调到同一个时间。

branches.en: Separate efforts are brought into one rhythm.
branches.cn: 分散的努力被带进同一个节奏。

branches.en: Numbers on a grid name one exact place.
branches.cn: 网格上的数字命名一个确切的位置。

branches.en: Two items stand side by side without one bowing.
branches.cn: 两样东西并排而立，谁也不必低头。

branches.en: Both depend on things being set in relation to each other.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖事物之间的相互关系。

branches.en: A coordinate tells where, and to coordinate tells when and how.
branches.cn: 坐标说明在哪里，协调说明何时与如何。

intro.en: Coordinate is built on Latin co-, together, plus ordinare, to set in order.
intro.cn: coordinate 由拉丁语 co-（一起）与 ordinare（排列）构成。

latinIntro.en: The ordering base ordin- also appears in order, ordinary and subordinate.
latinIntro.cn: 排列词基 ordin- 也出现在 order、ordinary 与 subordinate 中。

items.meaning: to set parts in one order
items.meaningCN: 把各部分排进同一顺序

items.meaning: a person who arranges joint work

items.meaningCN: 超出应有次序或限度的

definition_zh: 协调；配合；协调能力；并列关系
definition_en: the act of making parts work together, the ability to move smoothly, or a balanced link in grammar
core_image: 几根线在同一只手里被收拢，拧成一股结实的绳
scene: 救援现场最缺的不是人手，而是让各队同时行动的那份安排。Good coordination kept the teams from getting in each other's way.
sceneCN: 这里 coordination 指「协调；配合」（第 1 个义项：让不同部分协同运作）；句意是良好的协调让各队没有互相妨碍。

senses.title: The working of parts together
senses.definition: the act of organizing people or parts so that they work well together
senses.definitionCN: 把人员或部分组织起来使其配合良好的行为
senses.example: The rescue depended on close coordination.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援依靠紧密的协调。
senses.why: Many hands move faster only when they move on one plan.
senses.whyCN: 许多双手只有在同一份计划上才动得更快。

senses.title: Smooth control of the body
senses.definition: the ability to move different parts of the body smoothly together
senses.definitionCN: 让身体各部分顺畅配合的能力
senses.example: Dancing improved her coordination.
senses.exampleCN: 跳舞改善了她的协调能力。
senses.why: The body is also a team, and it too needs a manager.
senses.whyCN: 身体也是一支队伍，也需要一个调度者。

senses.title: A balanced grammatical link
senses.definition: a grammatical connection between two parts of equal rank
senses.definitionCN: 两个同级部分之间的语法连接
senses.example: The sentence uses coordination, not subordination.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子用的是并列关系，不是从属关系。
senses.why: Grammar also likes things to stand level, hand in hand.
senses.whyCN: 语法也喜欢让事物平起平坐、手拉着手。

intro.en: Coordination comes from Latin coordinatio, from coordinare, to arrange together, built from co-, together, and ordo, order.
intro.cn: coordination 来自拉丁语 coordinatio，源于 coordinare（一同排列），由 co-（一起）与 ordo（次序）构成。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, a rank or a fixed arrangement.
items.cn: ordo 意为行列、等级或固定的排列。

items.en: Coordinare meant to set several things into one arrangement.
items.cn: coordinare 意为把几样事物排进同一个安排。

items.en: Coordinatio named the state of being arranged together.
items.cn: coordinatio 指被一同排列的状态。

items.en: English coordination first described equal rank in logic.
items.cn: 英语 coordination 最初描述逻辑中的同级关系。

items.en: It now covers teamwork, muscles and grammar alike.
items.cn: 今天它同时涵盖团队协作、肌肉动作与语法关系。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ordering base ordin-, and the meaning group names other forms of joint effort.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的排列词基 ordin-，近义组列出其他表示共同出力的说法。

entries.definition: to make parts work together
a person who organizes joint work
the act of making someone a priest
the act of working with others
the arranging of things into a working whole
entries.definitionCN: 把事物安排成运作的整体

entries.definition: joint effort by a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with threads gathered into one hand, then move to a body moving as one and to clauses side by side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从几根线被收进一只手开始，再到身体像一个整体那样动，最后到并排的分句。

normal.en: Coordination is the noun behind coordinate: the result of setting things in one order.
normal.cn: coordination 是 coordinate 背后的名词：把事物排进同一顺序之后的成果。

normal.en: Think of a rowing crew: eight oars, one rhythm.
normal.cn: 想象一支赛艇队：八支桨，一个节奏。

normal.en: Hand-eye coordination is the same idea inside one body.
normal.cn: 手眼协调就是同一个道理，只是装在一个身体里。

normal.en: In grammar, coordination joins equals; subordination joins unequals.
normal.cn: 语法里，并列连接平等者，从属连接不平等者。

normal.en: The longer word carries the calmer, more official tone.
normal.cn: 这个词更长，语气也更沉稳、更正式。

abstract.en: Picture several threads closing into one knot.
abstract.cn: 想象几根线收拢成一个结。

abstract.en: Picture eight rowers pulling at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象八名桨手在同一瞬间发力。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers turning without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象两名舞者不说一句话就转身同步。

examples.en: The festival ran smoothly thanks to careful coordination.
examples.cn: 多亏细致的协调，节庆活动顺利进行。

examples.en: Her coordination improved after months of practice.
examples.cn: 练习几个月后，她的协调能力提高了。

examples.en: The plan was made in coordination with local schools.
examples.cn: 这项计划是与当地学校协同制定的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coordination 记成 co（一起）加 ordin（次序）加 ation：让各方进入同一个次序，就是协调。

root: 源自拉丁语 coordinare（一同排列）的名词 coordinatio，由 co-（一起）与 ordo（次序）构成，后引申为身体协调与语法并列。

sensesIntro.en: From many threads held in one hand, to a body moving as one, and at last to two clauses standing level.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只手拢住的许多线，到像一个整体那样动的身体，最后到并排而立的分句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several threads twisted into one strong cord.
core.cn: 核心意象：几根线被拧成一股结实的绳。

branches.en: Separate groups agree on one plan and one time.
branches.cn: 分开的群体就同一份计划与时间达成一致。

branches.en: Muscles and eyes learn to work as a single unit.
branches.cn: 肌肉与眼睛学会作为一个整体运作。

branches.en: Two equal parts are joined without either ruling.
branches.cn: 两个平等的部分相连，谁都不统治谁。

branches.en: Both senses are about smooth joint movement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎顺畅的共同动作。

branches.en: A body and a sentence both need balanced parts.
branches.cn: 身体与句子都需要彼此平衡的部分。

intro.en: Coordination is coordinate plus -ion, resting on Latin co-, together, and ordo, order.
intro.cn: coordination 是 coordinate 加 -ion，根源是拉丁语 co-（一起）与 ordo（次序）。

latinIntro.en: The ordering base ordin- also appears in order, ordinary and subordinate.
latinIntro.cn: 排列词基 ordin- 也出现在 order、ordinary 与 subordinate 中。

items.meaning: the joining of parts in one order
items.meaningCN: 把各部分排进同一顺序

items.exampleCN: 从属分句要依附别的分句。

definition_en: a police officer in informal speech, or to receive something unpleasant
core_image: 街角一个穿制服的身影，帽檐压得很低
scene: 夜里巷口有人吹了声口哨，穿制服的人转过身来。A cop stopped us at the corner and asked for our names.
sceneCN: 这里 cop 指「警察」（第 1 个义项：口语中对警察的称呼）；句意是一名警察在街角拦住我们，问我们的名字。

senses.title: A police officer
senses.definition: a police officer, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对警察的称呼
senses.example: A cop waved the traffic through.
senses.exampleCN: 一名警察挥手让车流通过。
senses.why: A short word feels closer to the street than the full title does.
senses.whyCN: 短短的称呼比正式头衔更贴近街头。

senses.title: To receive something bad
senses.definition: to get something unpleasant, such as a fine or blame
senses.definitionCN: 承受不愉快的事，如罚款或责骂
senses.example: He copped a fine for parking there.
senses.exampleCN: 他因在那里停车挨了罚款。
senses.why: When trouble lands on you, the verb makes you the catcher, not the chooser.
senses.whyCN: 麻烦落到头上时，这个动词让你成了接住的人，而不是挑选的人。

intro.en: Cop as a word for a police officer probably comes from copper, which may go back to the old verb to cop, to seize, from Latin capere.
intro.cn: cop 指警察，大概来自 copper，而 copper 可能追溯到古动词 cop（抓住），源于拉丁语 capere。

items.en: Capere meant to take hold of or seize.
items.cn: capere 意为抓住或拿住。

items.en: Old French caper kept the sense of seizing.
items.cn: 古法语 caper 保留了抓取的含义。

items.en: The slang verb to cop meant to catch or grab.
items.cn: 俚语动词 cop 意为抓住、逮住。

items.en: Copper became a common slang word for a police officer.
items.cn: copper 成为警察的常见俚语说法。

items.en: Cop shortened copper and spread through film and song.
items.cn: cop 缩短了 copper，并经电影与歌曲传播开来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short -op shape, and the meaning group names other words for police work.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 -op 外形，近义组列出其他与警察工作有关的词。

entries.definition: a thing made to look like another
entries.definitionCN: 照着另一件做出来的东西

entries.definition: to deal with a hard situation
a soft hat with a front part
a male member of the police
a person with authority in the police
a police officer who solves crimes

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a uniform at a corner, then move to a fine landing on someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从街角的制服开始，再到一笔罚款落到某人头上。

normal.en: One short syllable, like a whistle in the night.
normal.cn: 一个短促的音节，像夜里的一声口哨。

normal.en: Cop and copy both suggest taking something quickly.
normal.cn: cop 与 copy 都带着迅速拿走一点什么的感觉。

normal.en: The verb is the trouble half: you cop a fine, you cop the blame.
normal.cn: 动词是倒霉的那一半：挨罚款，背黑锅。

normal.en: Copper is the older, longer form of the same slang.
normal.cn: copper 是同一个俚语更早、更长的形式。

normal.en: Do not write it with two p's unless you add -ed or -ing.
normal.cn: 除非加 -ed 或 -ing，否则不要写成两个 p。

abstract.en: Picture a cap and a raised hand under a street lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象路灯下一顶帽子和一只抬起的手。

abstract.en: Picture a paper fine fluttering down onto a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张罚款单飘落到桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a whistle cutting through a quiet street.
abstract.cn: 想象一声哨响划破安静的街道。

examples.en: A cop on a bike followed the bus.
examples.cn: 一名骑车的警察跟着那辆公交车。

examples.en: She copped a fine for missing the deadline.
examples.cn: 她因错过期限挨了罚款。

examples.en: The manager copped all the blame.
examples.cn: 经理承担了所有责骂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cop 记成一声短哨：街角吹哨的人就是警察，而他抓住你时，你就得挨罚。

root: 源自拉丁语 capere（抓住），经古法语进入英语，先有动词 cop（逮住），再由 copper 缩短成 cop，口语中用来称警察。

sensesIntro.en: From the one who seizes, to the trouble that seizes you.
sensesIntro.cn: 从抓住别人的人，到抓住你的麻烦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a uniform and a cap at a street corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角的一身制服和一顶帽子。

branches.en: The one who seizes trouble is named by a short word.
branches.cn: 负责抓住麻烦的人，用一个短词来称呼。

branches.en: Trouble can also seize the ordinary person.
branches.cn: 麻烦也会抓住普通人。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the old idea of catching.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在抓取这个古老含义上。

branches.en: The noun is friendly or rude depending on the speaker.
branches.cn: 这个名词是亲切还是失礼，要看说话的人。

branches.en: The verb usually brings a fine, a blow or blame.
branches.cn: 这个动词带来的通常是罚款、打击或责骂。

intro.en: Cop goes back to Latin capere, to seize, through French, and gives English a short family of catching words.
intro.cn: cop 经法语上溯到拉丁语 capere（抓住），在英语里留下了一小族表示拿取的词。

latinIntro.en: The taking base cap- also runs through capture, captive, accept and capacity.
latinIntro.cn: 拿取词基 cap- 也贯穿 capture、captive、accept 与 capacity。

items.meaning: a slang word for a police officer
items.example: A copper stood by the door.

items.meaning: a thing taken from an original
items.meaningCN: 从原件拿下来的一份东西
items.example: Keep a copy of the letter.

items.meaning: to deal with a hard task
to take a person or place by force
items.meaningCN: 用武力抓住人或占领地方

items.example: The hall has a large capacity.

definition_en: to deal with a difficult situation or a heavy load
core_image: 一个人低着头顶着风走，衣角被吹得笔直
scene: 停水三天，邻居们轮流去远处打水。Some families coped by sharing water with their neighbours.
sceneCN: 这里 cope 指「应对」（第 1 个义项：面对困难局面并设法撑住）；句意是有些家庭靠与邻居分水来应对。

senses.title: To get through a hard time
senses.definition: to manage a difficult situation with the means you have
senses.definitionCN: 用手上有的办法撑过一个困难局面
senses.example: They coped with the loss of power for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们撑过了一个星期没电的日子。
senses.why: A storm does not ask whether you are ready; it asks whether you can stand.
senses.whyCN: 风暴不问你准备好没有，只问你能不能站住。

senses.title: To handle a task well enough
senses.definition: to deal with a problem or duty without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或职责处理得过去，而不至于崩掉
senses.example: She copes with three jobs and a family.
senses.exampleCN: 她要应付三份工作和一个家庭。
senses.why: Not every day is won; some are simply carried to the end.
senses.whyCN: 不是每一天都算赢，有些日子只是被撑到了尽头。

intro.en: Cope comes from Old French couper, to strike or cut, from Latin colaphus, a blow, from Greek kolaphos.
intro.cn: cope 来自古法语 couper（打、切），源于拉丁语 colaphus（一击），更早出自希腊语 kolaphos。

items.en: Kolaphos meant a blow with the fist.
items.cn: kolaphos 意为用拳头打的一击。

items.en: Colaphus kept the sense of a blow or a buffet.
items.cn: colaphus 保留了打击或掌击的含义。

items.en: Old French couper meant to strike or cut.
items.cn: 古法语 couper 意为击打或切割。

items.en: English cope first meant to fight or come to blows with someone.
items.cn: 英语 cope 最初意为与某人交手或打起来。

items.en: The sense shifted from fighting to handling a burden.
items.cn: 词义从打斗转向承担与应付。

items.en: Today it almost always appears with with.
items.cn: 今天它几乎总是与 with 一同出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short -ope shape, and the meaning group names other verbs for facing difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 -ope 外形，近义组列出其他面对困难的说法。

entries.definition: a thing made to match another
a police officer in informal speech
the range a subject or plan covers
entries.definitionCN: 某主题或计划覆盖的范围

entries.definition: to succeed in dealing with something
to deal with a situation or person
entries.definitionCN: 处理某种局面或某个人

entries.definition: to bear something painful for a long time

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a person walking into wind, then move to too many duties held at once.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个人逆风行走开始，再到同时压来的过多职责。

normal.en: Cope almost always travels with with, because no one copes alone with nothing.
normal.cn: cope 几乎总和 with 同行，因为没人能空着手独自应付。

normal.en: The old sense was to trade blows; now you trade blows with a problem.
normal.cn: 它古时指交手；现在你是和一个问题交手。

normal.en: Think of a small boat riding a big wave: it does not stop the wave.
normal.cn: 想象小船压过大浪：它没有让浪停下。

normal.en: Coping is not winning; it is staying afloat.
normal.cn: 应对不是取胜，而是还浮在水面。

normal.en: One letter away from copy, but nothing here is copied.
normal.cn: 它和 copy 只差一个字母，但这里没有什么是抄来的。

abstract.en: Picture a walker leaning into a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个行人倾身顶着大风。

abstract.en: Picture a table piled with boxes and one steady hand beneath.
abstract.cn: 想象堆满箱子的桌子下，有一只手稳稳托着。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge holding while the river pushes.
abstract.cn: 想象河水冲压时，一座桥仍然撑住。

examples.en: He copes with pressure by running every morning.
examples.cn: 他每天早晨跑步来应对压力。

examples.en: The staff coped well when the system failed.
examples.cn: 系统出故障时，员工应付得很好。

examples.en: Some students find it hard to cope with the pace.
examples.cn: 有些学生觉得难以应付这种节奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cope 记成一个人顶着风走：风不会停，能走过去就是应付。

root: 源自希腊语 kolaphos（一拳），经拉丁语 colaphus 与古法语 couper（击打）进入英语，本指交手，后转为承担与应付。

sensesIntro.en: From trading blows with an opponent, to standing under a load that will not lift.
sensesIntro.cn: 从与对手交手，到站在一份不会变轻的重担之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning into a hard wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人倾身顶着强风。

branches.en: A hard time is met with whatever means are at hand.
branches.cn: 困难时期，用手边有的办法去迎。

branches.en: A duty is carried through without collapse.
branches.cn: 一份职责被撑到最后，人没有垮。

branches.en: Both senses are about standing while pressure stays.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎压力仍在时站稳。

branches.en: The first is short and sharp, like a storm.
branches.cn: 第一个义项短而急，像一场风暴。

branches.en: The second is long and quiet, like a daily load.
branches.cn: 第二个义项长而静，像每天的负担。

intro.en: Cope reached English through Old French couper, to strike, from Latin colaphus, a blow.
intro.cn: cope 经古法语 couper（击打）进入英语，源于拉丁语 colaphus（一击）。

latinIntro.en: Cope keeps company with short look-alikes such as copy and cop rather than with a Latin base.
latinIntro.cn: cope 更多与 copy、cop 这类短小形近词为伴，而没有留下常用的拉丁词基。

items.meaning: the act or way of dealing with stress
items.meaningCN: 应对压力的行为或方式

items.meaning: an easy way of avoiding a duty

items.example: A copyist made the fair copy.
items.exampleCN: 一名抄写员誊出了定稿。

definition_zh: 铜；铜币；警察（英式口语）；铜色的
definition_en: a reddish brown metal, a coin made of it, or a British slang word for a police officer
core_image: 一截裸露的铜线在灯下泛出暖红的光
scene: 电工剥开电线外皮，露出一段发亮的金属。The wire is made of copper, so it bends easily.
sceneCN: 这里 copper 指「铜」（第 1 个义项：一种红棕色的金属）；句意是这根导线是铜做的，所以容易弯。

senses.title: The reddish metal
senses.definition: a soft reddish brown metal used for wires and pipes
senses.definitionCN: 一种柔软的红棕色金属，用于制线和管道
senses.example: Copper carries electricity very well.
senses.exampleCN: 铜的导电性很好。
senses.why: The metal was once dug on Cyprus, and the island gave it its name.
senses.whyCN: 这种金属曾在塞浦路斯开采，岛名就成了它的名字。

senses.title: A low value coin
senses.definition: a coin of small value, once made of copper
senses.definitionCN: 面值很小的硬币，早年用铜铸成
senses.example: He paid with a handful of coppers.
senses.exampleCN: 他付了一把铜币。
senses.why: Small money is named by the metal it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 小面值的钱，用铸它的金属来命名。

senses.title: A police officer in slang
senses.definition: a British slang word for a police officer
senses.definitionCN: 英式俚语中对警察的称呼
senses.example: A copper asked to see his licence.
senses.exampleCN: 一名警察要求看他的执照。
senses.why: The slang may come from the old verb to cop, to catch.
senses.whyCN: 这个俚语可能来自古动词 cop，意为抓住。

intro.en: Copper comes from Latin cuprum, a shortening of Cyprium aes, metal of Cyprus, where the ore was mined.
intro.cn: copper 来自拉丁语 cuprum，是 Cyprium aes（塞浦路斯的金属）的缩写，因为当地开采铜矿。

items.en: Kypros was the Greek name of the island of Cyprus.
items.cn: Kypros 是塞浦路斯岛的希腊语名称。

items.en: Cyprium aes meant the metal that came from Cyprus.
items.cn: Cyprium aes 意为来自塞浦路斯的金属。

items.en: Cuprum shortened the phrase and named the metal alone.
items.cn: cuprum 缩短了这个短语，单独指这种金属。

items.en: English borrowed the word as copor from Latin speakers.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语使用者那里借来了 copor 这个词。

items.en: The spelling settled toward copper, close to the modern form.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 copper，接近今天的形式。

items.en: Slang added the sense of a coin and of a police officer.
items.cn: 俚语又添上了铜币与警察两个含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short -op- shape, and the meaning group names other metals and alloys.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 -op- 外形，近义组列出其他金属与合金。

entries.definition: a police officer in informal speech
